questions.q: According to this lesson, why is Salesforce described as a "clicks-first" tool?
options: Because Salesforce cannot be customized at all
Because Trailhead only teaches programming languages
Because Apex code is required for every single configuration change
Most real admin work (fields, page layouts, security, Flow) is done by configuring through Setup, not by writing code
questions.explain: Salesforce admin work is overwhelmingly point-and-click configuration in Setup, which is why hands-on practice matters so much.

questions.q: What does this lesson say about the format of Salesforce certification exams?
options: They have no connection to real admin work
They only ask you to define vocabulary words
They require writing a full Apex trigger from memory
They are scenario-based, describing a business problem rather than asking you to define a term
questions.explain: Salesforce certification exams describe a business scenario and ask what you'd configure to solve it, which is why repetition in a real org matters.

questions.q: By the end of this chapter (Lessons 1-5), what will you have, per this lesson?
options: A sandbox copied from a production company's real customer data
A free Trailhead account and a Trailhead Playground, plus a clear understanding of how a Playground, Developer Edition org, and sandbox differ
A completed Salesforce Administrator certification
A paid Salesforce Enterprise Edition subscription
questions.explain: This chapter sets up a free Trailhead account and Playground, and clarifies the differences between a Playground, Developer Edition org, and sandbox.

questions.q: Why does this lesson argue that reading documentation alone isn't enough to prepare for the job?
options: Because Salesforce has no documentation available
Because recognizing which Setup page solves a stakeholder's problem only comes from repetition inside a real org, not from reading
Because documentation is always incorrect
Because reading is explicitly banned on the Salesforce exam
questions.explain: The lesson's core argument is that recognition and speed come from repeated hands-on practice, not from reading alone.

questions.q: Does setting up the free practice environment described in this chapter cost anything, according to this lesson?
options: Yes, but only the Trailhead account is free; the org itself always costs money
No — Salesforce deliberately keeps a free tier of real orgs available for people learning the platform
It's free for the first week only, then requires payment
Yes, it requires an Enterprise Edition subscription
questions.explain: The Trailhead account and Trailhead Playground this chapter sets up are both free, with no credit card required.
